reference_title: UFC 3-301-01, Structural Engineering (DoD, dated 11 April 2023, as amended through Change 4, 3 June 2025)
scope_note: All 13 numbered/captioned figures in the document, spanning Chapter 2 (Figure 2-1, Additively Constructed Concrete webbing detail), Chapter 3 (Figure 3-1, flexible-diaphragm wall anchorage), and Appendix C (Figures C-1 through C-11, nonstructural-component seismic-design details incl. the Table C-1/C-2/C-3 pipe-span support-condition figures). All pages resolved from the document's own PDF bookmark (TOC) destinations and cross-verified directly against the extracted page text at each location (printed_page = pdf_page_index - 21 throughout this document, confirmed at multiple anchor points from p.1 to p.206); page_estimated=false throughout. Figure C-9's multi-mode period-coefficient chart is cataloged but its coefficient values are NOT individually digitized in nonstructural_seismic.py (see the package __init__.py docstring gap note).

figures.caption: Webbing in Shell Elements
figures.description: Additively Constructed Concrete (3D-printed concrete) wall detail showing webbing employed between two printed concrete face shells to act compositely, per paragraph 1903.4 -- requires third-party load-test validation of the composite assembly for all relevant loading.

figures.caption: Anchorage of Walls to Flexible Diaphragm
figures.description: Determination of the flexible-diaphragm span Lf used in ASCE 7-22 Section 12.11.2.1 wall anchorage force calculations, per paragraph 3-6.4.

figures.caption: Partial Infill Masonry Wall between Two Concrete Columns, Causing Adverse "Short Column" Effect
figures.description: Illustrates the short-column effect at a partial infill wall (window strip above a solid infill panel between columns): the upper unbraced column segment becomes a stiff, shear-vulnerable 'short column' relative to the fully braced adjacent columns.

figures.caption: Typical Details for Isolation of Rigid Partition Walls
figures.description: Lateral-support details (continuous angles, hanger wires, L-brace, slotted connections) for isolating rigid nonstructural partition walls from in-plane building lateral forces; limited to SDC A/B/C per the source note.

figures.caption: Typical Seismic Restraints for Floor-mounted Equipment
figures.description: Base anchorage/restraint detail for floor- or pad-mounted equipment in Risk Category IV buildings, referenced by the Section C-3.1 base-mounted-equipment cast-in-place anchor bolt guidance.

figures.caption: Typical Seismic Restraints for Suspended Equipment
figures.description: Trapeze-hanger and diagonal-bracing details for suspended mechanical equipment, including a vibration-isolation-mount variant, per ANSI/SMACNA 001-2008 guidance referenced in Section C-3.1.

figures.caption: Acceptable Seismic Details for Pipe Sway Bracing
figures.description: Sway-bracing connection details (45-degree bracing, cast inserts, clip angles) for horizontal pipe supports per Section C-3.1.3.

figures.caption: Pinned-pinned Support Condition for Table C-1
figures.description: Support-condition diagram (span L, pinned-pinned) corresponding to the Table C-1 rigid-pipe maximum-span values.

figures.caption: Fixed-pinned Support Condition for Table C-2
figures.description: Support-condition diagram (span L, fixed-pinned) corresponding to the Table C-2 rigid-pipe maximum-span values.

figures.caption: Fixed-fixed Support Condition for Table C-3
figures.description: Support-condition diagram (span L, fixed-fixed) corresponding to the Table C-3 rigid-pipe maximum-span values.

figures.caption: Period Coefficients for Uniform Beams
figures.description: Fundamental-period mode-shape coefficients C for uniform cantilever (fixed-base) and pinned-base beams, used with Ta = C*L^2*sqrt(w/(EI)) for cantilever-stack period estimation (Section C-3.2.2). NOT individually digitized in nonstructural_seismic.py -- the per-mode-shape coefficient/deflected-shape pairing is ambiguous in the extracted text; consult the printed figure directly if higher-mode stack periods are needed.

figures.caption: Single Guyed Stacks
figures.description: Flexible-wire vs. rigid-wire deflected-shape comparison for a single guyed stack, illustrating why guy cables should be pretensioned to at least 10% of the stack's seismic force Fp (Section C-3.2.2).

figures.caption: Elevator Details
figures.description: Elevator car/counterweight frame, guide rail, roller-guide-assembly, and retainer-plate detail referenced by the Section C-3.3 elevator seismic-design criteria (guide-rail deflection limits, retainer-plate clearance, counterweight tie-bracket spacing).
